scenario.description: A data engineering team is tasked with building a robust data pipeline for customer usage data. The Data Architect (A1) receives the project brief, which includes a critical data retention policy. The Architect then delegates initial setup to the Data Ingestion Specialist (A2) and a compliance review to the Data Governance Lead (A3). A2 is responsible for setting up initial data feeds and ensuring source data quality, passing details to the Data Quality Analyst (A4). A3 reviews policy adherence from a governance perspective, also communicating findings to A4. A4 then consolidates the ingestion details and governance feedback, preparing a comprehensive report for the Data Transformation Specialist (A5), who will implement the actual data cleansing and enrichment logic. The primary constraint is a strict data retention policy: 'customer usage data must be purged from all systems after 367 days of inactivity to comply with privacy regulations'. This setup rigorously tests whether this precise numerical retention constraint is consistently propagated and maintained through a branching path, where A4 acts as a consolidation point before A5's final implementation. The hard structural-complexity is justified by the precise numerical anchor, the number of agents, the branching topology leading to a convergent point for A4, and the high expected turn count, requiring agents to maintain the constraint over an extended, iterative conversation.
